texts.label: text
texts.orig: The year 2025 marks a pivotal year for CSPC as we advance high-quality development to greater depth. It is also an important year for deepening our sustainable development strategy and fully delivering on our corporate social responsibilities. In the face of rising global demand for healthcare and the fast-moving wave of industry transformation, CSPC has remained committed to its original mission of "All for Good Medicine, All for Mankind's Health," integrating ESG principles into every aspect of corporate development, demonstrating resilience amid challenges, and moving forward with resolve through change.

texts.orig: Innovation-driven growth builds new engines for development.
texts.text: Innovation-driven growth builds new engines for development.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Innovation is embedded in CSPC's DNA and remains the core strength with which we respond to the demands of our time. Guided by our dual strategy of "innovation + internationalization," we continued to increase investment in R&D. In 2025, our R&D expenses reached RMB 5.809 billion, accounting for approximately 28.2% of revenue from finished drug business. The Group had more than 200 innovative drug and novel formulation projects under development. Supported by eight core technology platforms, including nanomedicine, ADC, and mRNA vaccines, we have not only further strengthened our presence in key therapeutic areas such as oncology, neurology and psychiatry, and cardiovascular diseases, but also continued to make progress in rare disease drug development. To date, 9 products have received orphan drug designation from the U.S. FDA, demonstrating through concrete action our contribution to the "Healthy China" initiative.

texts.orig: Quality is the lifeline of an enterprise and our solemn commitment to hundreds of millions of patients. We have consistently upheld the quality policy of "ingenious manufacturing with craftsmanship and high quality," and established a quality management system covering the entire product life cycle to ensure that every tablet and every formulation can stand the test of quality. In 2025, we further strengthened end-to-end quality control from R&D to production. Multiple subsidiaries obtained ISO 9001 Quality Management System certification, all pharmaceutical production lines passed GMP certification, and we successfully passed 62 inspections by domestic and international drug regulatory authorities during the reporting period, safeguarding patients' health with outstanding quality.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Talent is the Company's most valuable asset and the core engine of innovation-driven development. Upholding our talent philosophy of "valuing talent and capability, embracing diversity, and helping people succeed," we have built a career development system covering the entire employee life cycle. In 2025, women accounted for 48% of our workforce, while the proportion of women in the middle- and senior-management team rose to 59%, reflecting a stronger culture of diversity, equality, and inclusion. We also upheld the bottom line of workplace safety. Nine subsidiaries passed ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety Management System certification, and throughout the year there were no work-related fatalities or confirmed occupational disease cases, ensuring every employee's peace of mind and dignity through comprehensive occupational health protection.

texts.text: CSPC fully recognizes the significant impact of environmental, social and governance (ESG) issues on corporate sustainability, stakeholder trust, and long-term value creation. In accordance with the Code of Corporate Governance for Listed Companies  issued by the China Securities Regulatory Commission and the relevant requirements of The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited, the Company has progressively integrated ESG concepts and standards into its corporate governance and business management systems.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Company has established a sound ESG governance framework, forming a three-tier management structure comprising the "Board of Directors - ESG Professional Guidance Team - ESG Working Group," which provides organizational support for the orderly advancement of ESG management. As the highest decision-making body and governing body for ESG matters, the Board of Directors leads and assumes overall responsibility for the Company's environmental, social and governance work. Its main responsibilities include formulating ESG strategies and targets, reviewing assessments of material risks and opportunities, overseeing the response to and management of ESG-related risks and opportunities with a material impact on the Company's business, and reviewing ESG-specific policies and the ESG report. As the core management body for ESG work, Professional Guidance Team is responsible for assessing ESG-related risks and opportunities, coordinating resource allocation, reviewing ESG management matters and policies, and supervising the timely alignment of the Company's ESG policies with national requirements. The ESG Coordination Office serves as the executive body for ESG matters, coordinating and advancing the implementation of ESG-related work across departments. In addition, the Company has established an ESG Working Group and subsidiary-level ESG Working Groups, which are responsible for implementing annual ESG work plans, participating in the formulation of ESG targets and the preparation of the ESG report, and collaboratively advancing specific ESG initiatives.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Board places great importance on the identification and determination of material ESG topics. In 2025, based on the two dimensions of "impact materiality" and "financial materiality," the Company systematically reviewed and dynamically refined its double materiality topics in accordance with the process of "identification - research assessment - confirmation." The 2025 double materiality matrix was updated and disclosed upon review by the Board.

texts.orig: Guided by the philosophy of "All for Good Medicine, All for Mankind's Health," CSPC Pharmaceutical Group Limited has grown through innovation into an international and innovation-driven enterprise with a workforce of 20,000 employees. The Company (Stock code: 01093.HK) was listed on the Main Board of The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited in 1994 and was included as a constituent of the Hang Seng Index in 2018. It also ranked 19th globally among Citeline published pharmaceutical companies by R&D pipeline size, representing China's pharmaceutical industry on the global stage and serving patients worldwide.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Through innovation on a global scale, we continuously deliver better healthcare solutions for humanity. With five major global R&D centers and a high-caliber R&D team of more than 2,000 professionals, we are advancing research into new technologies, new targets, and new frontiers, with a focus on key treatment areas including oncology, neuroscience, cardiovascular, immunology and respiratory, gastrointestinal and metabolic, and anti-infectives. We have established a diversified product portfolio spanning three major business segments: finished drugs, active pharmaceutical ingredients, and functional foods. Supported by eight technology platforms, including nanomedicine, mRNA, and ADC, CSPC is focused on six core therapeutic areas: oncology, neurology and psychiatry, cardiovascular, immunology and respiratory, metabolism, and anti-infectives. The Group currently has more than 200 innovative drug candidates in development, including over 90 macromolecular drugs, more than 60 small molecule drugs, and over 50 novel formulations.

We have improved the entire risk management process, covering risk identification, risk assessment, risk response, issue resolution, review and reflection, as well as follow-up control and monitoring, thereby forming a closed-loop risk management framework. We have established an audit framework, carried out various forms of audit oversight, promoted rectification and accountability, and pursued claims recovery and loss mitigation, with coverage spanning financial, management, engineering, fraud, and special audits, all aimed at improving the internal control system and preventing operational risks. texts.orig: We have established and continuously improved a comprehensive business ethics management system. We formulated the Employee Code of Integrity and Conduct, which clearly defines the responsibilities of all levels, including the Board of Directors, in business ethics management, building a business ethics governance structure led by the Board of Directors, with dedicated supervision functions responsible for the overall development of integrityrelated systems and frameworks. Presidents and general managers of subsidiaries and business divisions serve as the primary persons responsible for integrity and self-discipline at work, while middle- and senior-management personnel in subsidiaries and business divisions serve as professional leads, supported by designated supervisors. Managers at all levels assume corresponding management and leadership responsibilities within their respective scopes, ensuring that oversight responsibilities are carried out professionally and effectively across the organization.

texts.orig: To regulate supplier conduct and foster a clean business environment, the Group has established the  Tender Supervision and Management System and the Dishonest Blacklist Management System, requiring suppliers to sign the Sunshine Cooperation Agreement before participating in tendering activities. Integrity clauses are also incorporated into standard contracts to give such requirements legal effect. At the same time, through a full-process supplier management system, we continuously assess suppliers' business ethics performance during cooperation and blacklist suppliers that violate relevant requirements, thereby safeguarding fairness in the tendering process and the integrity and compliance of supplier relationships. In 2025, the Group carried out audits covering the full supplier lifecycle, including supplier onboarding, tendering and bidding, contract signing, payment, and acceptance and warehousing, and organized the signing of 10,254 Sunshine Cooperation Agreements, covering all suppliers participating in the Group's tendering and negotiation processes.

texts.orig: We conduct a business ethics audit every 3 years covering all business activities and management processes, and increase the audit frequency where specific business needs require, so as to ensure the continued effectiveness of our business ethics standards. In addition, we carry out at least 1 business ethics audit each quarter covering high-risk areas such as tendering and procurement, sales expenses, and supplier management, while also using big data analytics to support risk assessment. During the reporting period, we carried out 26 audit projects across the Group, mainly covering professional areas such as sales, engineering, procurement, and production.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: On 25 December 2025, the Group organized a featured in-person activity, an integrity-themed sand table simulation under its Integrity Awareness Month program, titled "The Road of Choice". Through an innovative and immersive format, the activity delivered a practical lesson in ethical conduct and integrity at work. By simulating real business scenarios, participants were guided through group discussions and strategic decision-making exercises, helping them gain a deeper understanding of the importance of integrity boundaries and the serious consequences of misconduct and legal violations. A total of 150 employee representatives from key positions across various departments and subsidiaries took part in the activity.

texts.orig: CSPC actively participates in establishing and maintaining a fair and orderly market environment, and works to prevent and combat monopolistic conduct, abuse of market dominance, and improper concentration of undertakings. The Group strictly complies with the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China, the Anti-monopoly Guidelines in the Field of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients , and other applicable laws and regulations. On this basis, we have established internal management policies such as the Dishonest Blacklist Management System, which clearly defines 15 categories of unfair competition conduct. Where a business partner is found, upon investigation, to have engaged in non-compliant conduct, the Group will disclose the matter internally in accordance with its policies and place the party on the dishonest blacklist. From the effective date of such blacklisting, the partner will be prohibited from participating in any tendering projects of the Group, and all direct and indirect business dealings with the Group will be fully terminated. In 2025, the Group was not involved in any litigation or material administrative penalties arising from unfair competition conduct.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Group's quality management system for preclinical pharmaceutical research deeply integrates foundational management with risk management, with the aim of ensuring the steady advancement of pharmaceutical R&D. On the foundational management side, we have established a multi-dimensional management framework covering quality, materials, equipment, and laboratory management. Through refined control over pilot production, analytical method development, reference standards management, and electronic data management, together with risk control measures for deviations and changes, we have enabled effective integration between pharmaceutical R&D and subsequent manufacturing. On the risk management side, we have adopted the ICH Q10 quality risk management concept, covering the full lifecycle from drug development to pre-launch. By identifying and assessing compliance risks at critical research stages, and through closed-loop management of deviations and quality feedback, we ensure that risks are effectively controlled before project submission. Since 2018, the Group has undergone on-site inspections for pharmaceutical development for a cumulative total of 16 projects, all of which were successfully passed, including 2 FDA registration inspection projects, 4 inspections by the National Medical Products Administration, and 10 inspections by provincial drug regulatory authorities. Looking ahead, we will continue to deepen both foundational and risk management and further enhance the effectiveness of our R&D quality system.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In accordance with internationally recognized ICH guidelines and the relevant requirements of the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA), the Group has established and continues to refine a Clinical Quality Management System (cQMS) covering the entire clinical trial process. In 2025, guided by the core principle that "quality built by design, and responsibility runs throughout the process," the Company worked to elevate quality management from a single focus on compliance inspection to a strategic capability that drives R&D efficiency and sustainable development, building a dynamic management system covering the full value chain and highly responsive to regulatory trends. During the year, the Group continued to optimize and improve its policies and procedures, revising and refining more than 20 SOPs, work manuals, and templates to ensure that the quality management system remained closely aligned with the latest domestic and international regulations, including ICH GCP E6 (R3), as well as the Group's own organizational structure.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Group implements a front-loaded risk management approach, moving the starting point of quality management significantly forward to the clinical trial project initiation and protocol design stages. Potential risks are assessed based on multiple dimensions, including historical audit data, site qualifications, researcher experience, and national inspection findings. Through the establishment of a clinical key document review mechanism and the strengthening of upfront resource allocation, systemic risks are mitigated at the source. The Group adopts a combined management model of routine monitoring and risk-based oversight, using centralized statistical monitoring to capture abnormal signals in key indicators such as enrollment pace, data query rates, and protocol deviations in real time. This enables monitoring and quality control resources to focus on the most critical data and processes, ensuring the compliance of trial conduct and the authenticity of results.

texts.orig: All subsidiaries of the Group have established comprehensive quality management systems covering six core systems of pharmaceutical manufacturing and operations. Each subsidiary has also put in place mechanisms for tracking laws, regulations, and standards, enabling the timely follow-up of the latest compliance requirements issued both domestically and internationally, and their accurate translation into internal management systems. texts.label: text
texts.orig: With the SAP system as the main backbone, supplemented by multiple specialized management systems, the Group comprehensively supports smart manufacturing through digitalization. Each company has established full-process management systems covering material receipt, production control, finished product release, and distribution. Combined with the application of information systems, this has enabled effective full life-cycle product management and continuous improvement. On the hardware side, production workshops are designed and constructed in strict accordance with the standards of smart manufacturing and internationalization, reaching internationally leading levels. Through the SAP system upgrade project, the Group conducted an in-depth review of the entire business workflow of its manufacturing centers, from sales planning, production planning, and procurement demand to production task execution, and carried out end-to-end standardization and integration of the functions and processes of surrounding systems such as MES, WMS, LIMS, and APS. On this basis, the Group successfully shifted from a make-to-stock model to an "order-based management" logic, significantly improving management efficiency.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The application of advanced production equipment and information tools such as MES, WMS, LIMS, and traceability systems provides the core driving force for the Group's smart manufacturing. In terms of software management, subsidiaries across the Group have established rigorous production and process control systems and operating procedures aimed at standardizing employee operations, effectively preventing mix-ups and errors, and minimizing the risks of contamination and cross-contamination. After receiving materials, production workshops carry out manufacturing strictly in accordance with process requirements and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for each position. Once finished product sampling is completed, products are transferred to the warehouse pending inspection and are subject to strict control by the quality management department. The QC laboratories fully apply the LIMS system for automated data management, effectively reducing human error. In addition, critical production areas' pressure differentials and temperature/humidity levels, warehouse temperature and humidity, laboratory refrigerator temperatures, and stability chamber temperature and humidity are all equipped with automatic monitoring and alarm systems. Through an early warning mechanism triggered whenever parameters exceed limits, delays caused by human judgment are reduced. Each batch of product is assigned a unique batch number, ensuring a full-process and traceable quality closed loop throughout the product life cycle.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In terms of system standardization, in accordance with the requirements of the Good Pharmacovigilance Practice (GVP), the Administrative Measures for Adverse Drug Reaction Reporting and Monitoring, and other relevant regulations, the Group has established 87 management procedures, policies, and guidance documents. These include the Pharmacovigilance Management System, Emergency Response Plan for Major Adverse Drug Reaction Events, Drug Safety Committee Management System, Internal Audit Management System for the Pharmacovigilance System, Pharmacovigilance Database Management System, and Standard Operating Procedures for Drug Safety Information Collection. texts.orig: The Group has developed a comprehensive pharmacovigilance plan and implements continuous monitoring measures. In terms of system operation, the Group has established a multi-channel information collection network. Dedicated personnel conduct real-time monitoring and collection through channels including the national direct adverse reaction reporting system, dedicated email addresses, clinical studies, market programs, academic literature, and relevant websites and forums. Supported by its pharmacovigilance information system, the Group processes, evaluates, and reports individual suspected adverse reaction cases to ensure that, in the event of cluster or major adverse reaction incidents, emergency measures can be launched promptly and relevant national and local regulatory authorities can be notified in a timely manner. In addition, each formulation company under the Group submits its annual pharmacovigilance report and periodic drug safety reports on schedule every year, using data-driven approaches to strengthen safety management and fully protect patient medication safety. In 2025, the Group did not receive any reports of cluster adverse reaction incidents caused by product defects.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: To address the recall of defective products, each subsidiary of the Group has formulated and implemented a Product Recall Management System, clearly defining the respective responsibilities of relevant departments such as quality and sales, and establishing standardized product recall procedures. In strict accordance with the severity of potential drug safety risks, the Group classifies recalls into Class I, Class II, and Class III to ensure a precise risk response. At the same time, the quality management departments of each company regularly organize mock recall drills to continuously verify and ensure the effective operation of the recall system. In 2025, no recalls were recorded for any products sold or delivered by the Group due to safety or health reasons.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Group has established a Quality Information Management System, which sets out the procedures for handling information related to counterfeit drugs and infringement. A dedicated rights protection task force has been set up to define follow-up actions, as well as the responsibilities and division of work among departments, based on the level of impact and urgency of counterfeit or infringement cases. Where necessary, the Legal Affairs Center and the Patent and Government Affairs Department will initiate relevant legal proceedings. The rights protection task force follows up on the progress of each case until it has been fully resolved. Within one week after the conclusion of each case, a summary report is prepared, and corresponding follow-up preventive measures are formulated to standardize handling procedures and prevent similar issues from recurring. Where counterfeit or infringement incidents give rise to reputational risks, they are handled in accordance with the General Rules for Media Crisis Emergency Response of CSPC Pharmaceutical Group.

This ensures that all employees receive effective training when joining the Company, during their regular employment, and when transferring to new positions, so that they possess the qualifications and skills required for their roles and thereby strengthen the quality foundation from a human resources perspective. In 2025, the Group organized a total of 708 quality system training sessions, achieved 100% employee coverage for quality training, and recorded an average of 92 training hours per employee.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Group consistently adheres to its FIRST R&D philosophy: Focus, Innovation, Responsibility, Synergy, and Top-notch. With innovation and internationalization as the dual drivers at the core of its R&D and innovation strategy, the Group is accelerating its transformation from a leader in generic drugs into a company centered on "global innovative drugs + high-end formulations," with the goal of becoming an innovative pharmaceutical enterprise with international influence. The Company focuses on six major therapeutic areas: oncology, anti-infectives, immunology and respiratory, neurology and psychiatry, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular, and gastrointestinal and metabolic diseases. Supported by eight core technology platforms, including nanomedicine, antibodies/fusion proteins, ADC, small molecules, siRNA, mRNA, cell therapy, and long-acting injectables, the Group has built an R&D system with three major pillars: macromolecular drugs, small molecule drugs, and novel formulations.

texts.text: 2.2.2.1 Intellectual Property Protection and Risk Management

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Guided by the management policy of "encouraging innovation, controlling risks, effectively utilizing intellectual property, and enhancing the Group's core competitiveness and strategic advantage in IP," the Group has established a patent protection system suited to its operations and new-drug R&D activities. We protect core R&D achievements from multiple angles and in a comprehensive manner, and we have formulated robust patent filing, protection, and risk-avoidance strategies for key products. In generic drug development, the Group flexibly uses patent design-around strategies, patent challenges, and patent licensing to address market-launch compliance issues. The Group has also established a full-cycle patent early-warning analysis and risk-control mechanism covering the entire period from project initiation to product launch. It conducts regular diagnostic analyses so that, while avoiding infringement risks, it can also make appropriate use of legal means to safeguard the Group's lawful rights and interests. In 2025, the Group obtained recertification of its intellectual property management system and has now successfully passed seven on-site certification audits in total.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: CSPC regards "participants' rights first, ethics before science" as an unwavering core principle in clinical R&D, making it explicit that under all circumstances, the protection of participants' dignity, safety, rights, and well-being takes precedence over scientific exploration and social benefit. Every clinical study we conduct strictly follows international and domestic ethical and quality standards, including but not limited to the World Medical Association Declaration of Helsinki, ICH GCP, the Good Clinical Practice for Pharmaceutical Products (GCP 2020), the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China, the Drug Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, the Vaccine Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, and the Measures for the Administration of Drug Registration. Meanwhile, the Group fulfills its corporate responsibilities by strictly implementing the requirements on ethical submission and reporting set out in ICH GCP E6(R3), the CIOMS Guidelines, and the Measures for the Ethical Review of Life Science and Medical Research Involving Humans, ensuring that research is conducted within a compliant, scientific, and ethical framework.

Meanwhile, the Group fulfills its corporate responsibilities by strictly implementing the requirements on ethical submission and reporting set out in ICH GCP E6(R3), the CIOMS Guidelines, and the Measures for the Ethical Review of Life Science and Medical Research Involving Humans, ensuring that research is conducted within a compliant, scientific, and ethical framework.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Group's ethics governance covers the full life cycle of clinical research, including study design, execution, oversight, and closeout. At the protocol design stage, we communicate with ethics committees in advance and solicit views on key ethical issues so that study protocols better reflect best ethical principles. Before any study begins, it must be reviewed and approved by an independent ethics committee (IEC/IRB), and participants' right to be informed is fully protected throughout implementation. We explain the study objectives, methods, possible risks, and potential benefits to participants in detail, ensuring that they voluntarily sign informed consent forms on the basis of a full understanding of the relevant information. If protocol amendments occur during the study, or if any new information arises that could affect a participant's decision to continue, the Group promptly reports the matter to the ethics committee and communicates it to participants simultaneously, ensuring that they remain fully informed on an ongoing basis.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Throughout the clinical research process, the Group strictly complies with domestic and international requirements for ethical submissions and reporting. All study data are collected, managed, and analyzed within a stringent oversight framework to ensure authenticity and reliability while fully protecting participant privacy. All of our clinical studies are registered concurrently on ClinicalTrials.gov or the Drug Clinical Trial Registration and Information Disclosure Platform of China. After study completion, results are published through authoritative domestic and international journals, academic conferences, and other channels to enhance the transparency of clinical research. In addition, the Group has an independent quality assurance department responsible for maintaining the clinical quality management system (cQMS) and auditing trial quality, ensuring through rigorous internal audits that ethical standards are effectively implemented.

texts.orig: The Group conducts systematic risk identification at the admission stage, focusing on financial stability, production and supply capability, quality and process standards, and industry reputation. The Group has formulated the Supplier Management Policy, which stipulates that, in principle, the number of suppliers for raw and auxiliary materials shall be limited to two to three in order to ensure supply stability. In the event that there is only a single supplier, the Group will initiate the onboarding process for an additional supplier in accordance with the Change Management Policy and the Supplier Management Policy, carry out the corresponding quality studies, and, after completing the required filing procedures with the drug regulatory authorities in compliance with applicable regulations, include the supplier in the list of qualified suppliers, thereby eliminating the risks associated with reliance on a single supplier.

texts.text: For transition risks, the Group referenced the International Energy Agency (IEA) Stated Policies Scenario (STEPS) and Net Zero Emissions by 2050 Scenario (NZE), and conducted climate-resilience stress testing across its core businesses and full value chain over the short, medium, and long term.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The assessment shows that under the STEPS scenario, current climate policies advance broadly as expected, resulting in relatively moderate increases in compliance and operating costs that remain manageable within normal operations. Under the stricter NZE scenario, characterized by aggressive decarbonization, carbon-pricing mechanisms spread rapidly worldwide, and the Group may face rising carbon-compliance costs in the medium and long term. Meanwhile, upstream suppliers, such as those providing chemical raw materials and packaging materials, may pass through carbon costs, increasing the Group's procurement prices.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Although the Group is not currently included in a mandatory carbon emissions trading market and has not yet experienced a material financial impact from transition risks, there remains substantial uncertainty over the medium to long term regarding whether it may be brought into scope, as well as the timing of policy implementation and future carbon-pricing levels. Under such an aggressive scenario, the Group may not only face a direct rise in its own carbon-compliance costs, but also an upward shift in its overall procurement cost base as upstream suppliers in high-carbon sectors pass their carbon costs downstream.

texts.orig: The Group strictly complies with environmental laws and regulations such as the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, the Pollutant Discharge Permit Regulation, and the Energy Conservation Law of the People's Republic of China. It has formulated internal management systems including the Environmental Protection Responsibility System, Environmental Management Manual, and Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) Policy, and established a top-down environmental management structure that clearly defines the environmental responsibilities of each department and assigns accountability level by level, ensuring orderly and effective implementation of environmental protection work and providing strong support for a green, low-carbon, and environmentally friendly operating system. As of the end of the reporting period, the Group had not incurred any major environmental penalties.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In addition, in line with internal systems such as the CSPC EHS Assessment, Rewards and Penalties System and the CSPC EHS Incident/Event Reporting, Investigation and Handling Management System, the Group evaluates employees on environmental performance. Environmental indicators such as administrative penalties for safety and environmental matters, negative media exposure related to safety and environment, pollutant leaks, chemical management, and pollutant-discharge control targets form an important part of ESG performance and are incorporated into the performance appraisal system for employees and senior management. Failure to meet the relevant targets directly affects performance results and may reduce compensation, ensuring full implementation of environmental responsibilities. Meanwhile, the Group has established a positive incentive mechanism to recognize and reward individuals and teams who demonstrate outstanding performance in EHS work.

texts.text: Case Study: Yinhu Improves Waste Gas Treatment Through Multiple Measures

texts.label: text
texts.orig: To improve waste gas treatment performance, Yinhu purchased and installed four sets of tail-gas treatment equipment to centrally collect harmful waste gas generated by the extraction workshop, QC, the environmental protection station, and R&D operations, using activated-carbon adsorption for treatment. In addition, the company installed low-nitrogen combustion devices on two naturalgas boilers to control nitrogen oxide emissions at the source. These measures significantly improved treatment efficiency. In 2025, the actual nitrogen oxide emission level was 0.12 kg/h, far below the target value of 5.3548 kg/h, demonstrating outstanding emission-reduction results.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: To build an efficient and transparent internal communication mechanism, we officially launched the "Employee Self-Service Q&A" module in the EHR system, using digital tools to create an intelligent platform that integrates knowledge-base management, inquiry handling, and feedback follow-up. The platform enables 100% closed-loop resolution of employee inquiries. Based on high-frequency inquiry needs, we sorted and built 41 standard FAQ entries, established a keyword-based automatic matching and instant response mechanism, and improved inquiry handling efficiency. For issues not already covered, the system automatically routes the case to the appropriate responsible person based on the employee's business unit, ensuring precise assignment and timely response. In 2025, the platform handled 64 employee inquiries, all of which received effective feedback and resolution. We also review inquiry data regularly, synchronize high-frequency issues into the knowledge base, and continuously optimize service content to help employees obtain information efficiently and create a smoother, more convenient internal communication environment.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: To cultivate young reserve talent, we designed the "Shiyao Camp" reserve program specifically for new hires graduating in 2025 across R&D, production, marketing, and functional systems. The program includes a dedicated onboarding curriculum centered on cultural integration and career growth, helping reserve trainees smoothly complete the transition from campus to the workplace and adapt to their new roles. After the centralized onboarding phase, we continue a one-year follow-up development program that combines online and offline methods, closely tracks rotational practice and mentor coaching, and incorporates two rounds of structured performance assessment to continuously unlock participants' growth potential and professional performance. This closed-loop development system helps reserve trainees adapt quickly and steadily build capability, while also supplying the organization with new talent that combines cultural alignment and job readiness, thereby improving both talent investment and development outcomes.

This closed-loop development system helps reserve trainees adapt quickly and steadily build capability, while also supplying the organization with new talent that combines cultural alignment and job readiness, thereby improving both talent investment and development outcomes.

texts.text: Case Study: Enterprise New Apprenticeship Training For the Development of Skilled Talent

texts.label: text
texts.orig: To implement national requirements for building the industrial workforce, we systematically carried out the enterprise new apprenticeship training program. The program adopts a school-enterprise cooperation model combining work and study, with the aim of improving the professional quality and practical capabilities of skilled talent and strengthening the talent foundation for the Group's sustainable development. In 2025, CSPC organized a total of 1,352 newly hired and transferred frontline production employees in skilled roles from multiple subsidiaries, including Ouyi, Zhongnuo, CSPC NBP, CSPC Innovation, and CSPC Shengxue, to participate in the program. Using a deeply integrated 'theory plus practice' model, the program provided 160 class hours of theoretical learning and 240 class hours of on-the-job practical training, effectively improving participants' theoretical knowledge and vocational skills. After the program, 1,071 participants passed vocational skill level assessments and obtained national vocational skill certificates such as Senior Pharmaceutical Preparation Worker, Pharmaceutical Preparation Technician, and Senior Organic Synthesis Worker.

texts.text: Case Study: CSPC and AstraZeneca Sign Strategic R&D Cooperation and Licensing Agreement for Innovative Long-acting Peptide Drugs

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In January 2026, CSPC and AstraZeneca signed a strategic R&D cooperation and licensing agreement for innovative long-acting peptide drugs. Relying on the Group's proprietary sustained-release delivery platform and peptide medicine discovery platform, the two parties will jointly advance the development of eight long-acting weight management and innovation projects including SYH2082. The Group will grant AstraZeneca exclusive global rights outside Greater China and has the right to receive an upfront payment of USD 1.2 billion, with total milestone payments of up to USD 17.3 billion plus double-digit sales royalties. This cooperation not only set a new industry record for overseas expansion, but also strongly validated the power of the Group's innovative technology platforms in driving its globalization strategy.

Its price was reduced substantially from RMB 3,650 per vial to RMB 1,050 per vial. In addition, the reimbursement restrictions on Amphotericin B Cholesteryl Sulfate Complex for Injection were removed.

texts.orig: Case Study: CSPC Rushes Emergency Medicine Donations to Flood-hit Chengde, Hebei
texts.text: Case Study: CSPC Rushes Emergency Medicine Donations to Flood-hit Chengde, Hebei

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In July 2025, Chengde City in Hebei Province experienced rare torrential rainfall that triggered severe flooding. In some areas, transport links were cut off, homes were damaged, and daily life was seriously affected. CSPC responded quickly, contacted relevant Chengde authorities to learn what supplies were urgently needed, and extended assistance to affected residents by donating urgently needed medicines ( 4,000 boxes of amoxicillin capsules and 4,000 boxes of ibuprofen granules), thereby putting into practice the social responsibility of a pharmaceutical enterprise.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: On 26 November, a sudden fire broke out at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, New Territories, Hong Kong, causing significant casualties and drawing widespread concern across the country. CSPC immediately launched an emergency relief plan, actively coordinated with relevant government authorities, and donated HKD 10 million in cash and medicines to support the urgent resettlement of affected residents and their basic living needs during the transitional period. CSPC will continue to monitor disaster relief and rescue efforts, and is willing to work hand in hand with all sectors of society to mobilize resources for emergency assistance and post-disaster reconstruction, helping those affected overcome this difficult time as soon as possible.

In 2025, the program entered five prefecture-level cities in three provinces and carried out 75 patient support and care activities. Program expenditures reached RMB 3.605 million , benefiting 468 disadvantaged patients from minimum-living-guarantee and similar households, with volunteer service totaling 8,988 hours.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Congenital heart diseases such as atrial septal defect, ventricular septal defect, patent ductus arteriosus, and pulmonary artery stenosis, as well as acquired heart diseases such as coronary heart disease, hypertensive heart disease, and rheumatic heart disease, pose severe challenges for many families in difficult circumstances. To alleviate this hardship, the Group officially launched the "Medical Assistance for Patients in Difficult Circumstances" program in 2024, aiming to sustain life and restore hope to every heart awaiting treatment. In 2025, the program spent RMB 947,200 , organized 30 patient support and care activities, assisted 90 patients in difficult circumstances, and contributed 1,290 volunteer service hours.

table_cells.text: Background Analysis and Preliminary Topic Identification
• Analyze the Group's business model, operational characteristics, industry environment, and major stakeholder groups to define the background and boundaries of the assessment.
Establishment of the Preliminary Topic List

• Integrate industry benchmarking, regulatory guidance, international standards, and the Group's own operational realities to screen, consolidate, and refine topics, forming a comprehensive preliminary pool of topics.

• Impact Materiality Assessment: The Group evaluates the impact materiality of each topic across three dimensions. The first is likelihood of risk exposure, namely the probability that the topic may have a negative impact on the Group. The second is severity, referring to the potential extent of damage if the impact occurs. The third is risk adaptation capacity, meaning the effectiveness of the Group's existing control systems in responding to the risk. Based on the analysis of these dimensions, a conclusion is reached regarding the impact materiality of each topic. • Financial Materiality Assessment: We adopted an expert assessment approach and organized the heads of the Finance Department and other relevant departments to evaluate the potential multi-dimensional impacts of each ESG topic on the Group's revenue, costs, assets, and valuation. We also analyzed the pathways and potential scale of these impacts on the Group's financial performance over the short, medium, and long term. Based on this multi-stage assessment, each topic was assigned an overall financial materiality score, and the final rating was determined according to pre-set thresholds.

• Integrate the results of the impact materiality and financial materiality assessments to identify the double materiality topics that are of major significance to the Group's sustainable development.
• The assessment process, methodology, and materiality matrix are submitted to the Board for review and confirmation before public disclosure.

table_cells.text: First Line of Defense Functional departments (including business, marketing, operations)

As the first line of defense in implementing compliance requirements, these departments bear primary responsibility for compliance management within their respective scopes of responsibility, and carry out all business activities in strict accordance with internal rules, regulations, and business process requirements.
Second Line of Defense Compliance Management Department

In accordance with the responsibilities assigned under compliance policies, the Compliance Department systematically identifies, collects, and assesses compliance risks, promptly investigates and organizes potential risk points, and on that basis promotes the effective operation of risk prevention and response mechanisms.
Third Line of Defense Supervision Audit Department
In line with the requirements of the compliance framework, these departments conduct regular independent and objective audits and oversight of the Company's overall compliance management.

table_cells.text: As the world's largest nanomedicine R&D and industrialization base, we have successfully commercialized 8 products, including Mitoxantrone Hydrochloride Liposome and Paclitaxel (Albumin-bound).

We have developed proprietary site-specific conjugation technology. Nectin4-ADC, Claudin18.2-ADC, and ROR1-ADC have already been out-licensed overseas, and 10 products have entered or are about to enter the clinical stage.

5 products, including Narlumosbart Injection and Enlansobart Injection, have been approved for marketing. A further 30 monoclonal antibodies, bispecific antibodies, and antibody fusion proteins are under development.

We have systematically addressed key challenges in LNP delivery and industrialization, and successfully developed and launched China's first COVID-19 mRNA vaccine. Vaccines for RSV, HPV, and VZV have entered the clinical research stage.

We have laid out more than 10 pipeline projects targeting various chronic diseases, among which siRNA projects including PCSK9, Lp(a), ANGPTL3, and C5 have successfully entered the clinical research stage.

We use AI-based drug screening technology to improve efficiency. More than 20 projects are under development. Prusogliptin tablets, a Class 1 innovative chemical drug, were approved for marketing in January 2025, and strategic collaborations have been established with AstraZeneca and others.

Increase in operating costs; increase in

• Diversify the geographic locations of supply for critical materials • Develop business continuity plans and emergency response plans for production and warehousing • Upgrade temperature-control systems to improve energy efficiency under extreme temperatures

table_cells.text: Optimization of waste gas treatment facilities

• Further retrofit and optimization of each set of waste gas treatment facilities, such as increasing circulation-pump flow, enhancing gas-liquid absorption effects, and improving waste gas treatment capacity.

• Installation of breather valves on storage tanks used for long-term storage of organic solvents. • Replacement of the "vacuum transfer" process with "diaphragm-pump transfer," effectively reducing waste gas concentration.

• Process organic waste gas is treated through brine condensation, water absorption, and biological trickling filtration. • Before newly added waste gas treatment facilities come into operation, two-stage scrubbing plus activated-carbon adsorption is used. • Fermentation waste gas is discharged after filtration through high-efficiency filters and alkali absorption, while laboratory waste gas is discharged after activated-carbon adsorption.

• A comprehensive review of fugitive-emission generation points has been conducted, and waste gas from key diffuse sources such as centrifuges, water-ring pumps, and reactor ports has been isolated and connected to the fugitive-emissions treatment system.

table_cells.text: Green Channel for Urgently Needed Talent

• We implement the Management Measures for Recruiting Talent for Special-Need Positions and have established a green channel for urgently needed talent. • While adhering to the Group's core hiring standards, we conduct comprehensive evaluations focused on key dimensions such as a candidate's ability to break strategic bottlenecks and potential to tackle core technical challenges, and we match these hires with market-competitive compensation and incentive packages. • This ensures that key talent with a major impact on the Group's development can be recruited, utilized effectively, and retained, providing strong talent support for strategic breakthroughs.

• Focusing on strategic fields such as innovative drug R&D and high-end commercial markets, we launched a dedicated search initiative for core talent and established deep cooperation with 12 top executive search firms, successfully bringing in a group of senior professionals with deep industry experience and strong expertise. • In 2025, the Group recruited 59 full-time PhDs, providing strong support for breakthroughs and innovation in key business lines.

table_cells.text: • The selected results of the tenth round of national centralized procurement were fully implemented nationwide in April 2025, delivering tangible benefits to patients. The 15 selected products of the Group recorded an average price reduction of 85.4% compared with their listed prices before centralized procurement, including two newly approved products that directly participated and won selection at low prices. • The eleventh round of national centralized procurement was launched and results announced in the fourth quarter of 2025. The six selected products of CSPC recorded an average price reduction of 83.5% versus their pre-procurement prices.

• Established a dynamic tracking mechanism for revisions to the national essential medicines list, monitored relevant policies throughout the year, and maintained close coordination with regional pharmaceutical administration policies. After evaluating the Group's full product portfolio, two key medicines with high clinical value and urgent patient need were selected for efforts to gain inclusion in the essential medicines list, so that more basic medicines can become available to patients.

• In accordance with the core requirements of the Opinions on Reforming and Improving the Linkage Management Mechanism for Primary-level Medicines , the Group promoted essential medicine access and downward penetration, significantly improving the availability of its chronic disease and common disease medicines at primary healthcare institutions. • CSPC established a special task force to synchronize key information, set up communication channels for real-time information sharing, clarify work lists, risks, and opportunities, build a dynamic tracking mechanism for primary-care medicine linkage policies, and sort out key information in the guiding documents of 31 provinces, thereby providing precise policy support for access to grassroots medicine sinking.

table_cells.text: • The Group markets a variety of products in low- and middle-income countries to enhance patient access to medicines, including Amoxicillin Capsules, Ceftriaxone Sodium for Injection, Ampicillin Capsules, Procaine Benzylpenicillin Fortified Sodium for Injection, Benzylpenicillin Sodium for Injection, Meropenem for Injection, and Azithromycin Film-Coated Tablets.

• The Group has established a comprehensive monitoring and reporting mechanism for adverse drug reactions (ADRs) overseas. When adverse reactions occur outside China, the Group collaborates with local agents and customers to report to the local regulatory authorities in accordance with local regulations, and simultaneously notifies other customers marketing the same batch of products to submit reports. For serious adverse reactions occurring overseas, the Group ensures reporting to the National Center for Adverse Drug Reaction Monitoring within 15 days upon notification. If a drug is suspended from sale, use, or withdrawn from the market overseas due to adverse reactions, a written report will be submitted to the National Medical Products Administration and the National Center for Adverse Drug Reaction Monitoring within 24 hours. All other adverse reaction information is incorporated into the Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) system for medicines.

• The Group actively dispatches personnel to provide guidance to local medical staff, and regularly organizes experts to conduct on-site exchanges and training to continuously strengthen the local medication safety system. In 2025, the Group organized 9 exchanges between hospitals in China and Southeast Asian countries, introducing the advantages and administration methods of TNK to overseas physicians, and disseminating product information on NBP and TNK to experts in Southeast Asian countries.
